global_caption: The video contains 8 shots. It is a short tutorial-style video in realistic style, overall rendered in warm tones. Natural light from the evening city corner and soft warm reflections from the café table surface run throughout the footage. The emotional tone remains consistently relaxed and focused.
shot1: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in, wide eye-level shot. The café table at the street corner is centered slightly lower in the frame. Foreground features wooden table texture, background shows the street warmed by sunset and slowly moving traffic. A full box of building block parts is neatly placed on the table, forming a visual focal point. Depth of field is moderate, allowing environment recognition without distracting from the subject. A young woman sits beside the table, smiling toward the tabletop, ready to begin. Sunset natural light from the backside outlines her silhouette and part edges. The camera slowly pushes forward, helping viewers first establish the location and all materials.
shot2: Shot 2 follows with a hard cut from the previous shot, medium close-up, eye-level with slight overhead angle. Composition focuses on her hands and the opened box lid. The tabletop is divided into several clear zones: baseplate on the left, red bricks and long bricks in the center, window panels, door frames, and small pieces on the right. Background and foreground relationships are simple. Warm natural light casts soft highlights on the parts' surfaces. After opening the box, she quickly and accurately sorts parts by color. Her fingers pick up parts with clean, decisive movements. The camera makes a minimal downward tilt, enhancing step readability.
shot3: Shot 3 transitions via hard cut to extreme close-up overhead. The baseplate occupies most of the frame, red long bricks aligned along grid lines creating clear leading lines. Shallow depth of field makes the clip connections the absolute focus. Sunset warm light and table reflections remain consistent. After securing the baseplate in the center, she attaches long bricks one by one to build the foundation. When pressing down with fingertips, slight deformation, rebound, and the moment of clip engagement are visible. The camera slowly pushes in to emphasize precise interaction.
shot4: Shot 4 connects with a hard cut, medium eye-level shot with horizontal pan. The frame sweeps from left to right across the forming house base and her stable hands. Table edge and street railing create horizontal leading lines. Background traffic is slightly blurred. Warm lighting remains uniform. She builds both side walls symmetrically, aligning holes first before pressing down firmly. Wall height increases gradually. Brick alignment is clearly visible. The panning shot follows her hand movements, highlighting continuity and spatial relationship.
shot5: Shot 5 enters with a brief hard cut into near-extreme close-up, eye-level with slight upward tilt to enhance three-dimensionality of window panels and door frame. Foreground shows one completed wall edge. Focus rests on her fingertips holding transparent window panel and door frame slot. Glass-like window reflects sunset, creating tiny warm light spots. She installs the window panel first, then aligns the door frame, embedding both securely into the wall. Movements are meticulous, pausing briefly to confirm fit. Contact edges between hands and parts are clearly defined. The camera makes a slight push-in to emphasize installation details.
shot6: Shot 6 connects with a fade cut, overhead full close-up. The image is as clear as a tutorial diagram. The top of the house is centered, roof parts and streetlamp accessories arranged above in blank space. Wood grain and part layout form clean order. Warm daylight remains even. She first completes the roof, then inserts streetlamp pieces into street-side positions. Parts transition from scattered to fully connected. Roof outline and street accessories instantly complete the model. The camera remains stable overhead, only making minimal zoom-in to ensure every step is visible.
shot7: Shot 7 connects with a hard cut, medium eye-level shot with slow push-in. Composition places the finished small house slightly forward in center. Both her face and hands are within focus. Background is warmly blurred street with moving light spots. She checks each clip connection with fingertips, gently pressing roof, corners, window frames, and base. Then she gently adjusts a slightly crooked wall to vertical. Model state transitions from “完成但待确认” to “整齐稳固”. Her gaze is focused, lips slightly smiling. Camera push-in enhances confirmation feeling of “检查完成”.
shot8: Shot 8 follows with a natural pull-out transition, medium-long eye-level shot with slow pull-out. The young woman lifts the completed miniature street scene house with both hands to chest level for display. Finished product is centered. Foreground remains café table. Background shows street under sunset glow and slowly passing traffic. Warm light from side-back casts soft rim light on model edges. Composition unifies finished product, her smile, and urban life backdrop into a complete conclusion.
